newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal repo rate seen 6.80-7.00 pct by end-96.
newsitem.headline: Portugal repo rate seen 6.80-7.00 pct by end-96.

text.p: The Bank of Portugal, which trimmed its repo rate by 15 basis points (bp) to 7.10 percent on Thursday, has room to cut the rate further to between 6.80 and 7.00 percent by the end of the year, analysts said.

"If optimism over Portugal's chances of qualifying for the European single currency persists, if the escudo continues to rise and if inflation eases in the coming months as expected, the Bank of Portugal will cut its rates again," Isabel Cabral, economist with Lisbon broker Fincor, told Reuters.
"At the end of the year we could have a draining rate of 6.50 percent and a repo rate of between 6.90 and 7.0 percent," she added. The draining rate is now 6.80 percent.

An analyst with a bank said: "The Bank of Portugal was prudent again today, but it has room to lower the repo rate further this year, perhaps towards 6.80 percent after the approval of the 1997 budget."

The Portuguese bond market had expected a cut in the repo rate of between 25 and 50 basis points on Thursday after the Bank of Spain cuts its key money market interest rate earlier by 50 basis points to 6.75 percent.
But some Portuguese analysts had warned the Bank of Portugal could delay a cut in the repo rate until it was confident that inflation was on a firm downward path after creeping up over the summer.
Portuguese and Spanish bonds have surged recently on optimism that the two countries would qualify to join a single European currency in 1999.

Six analysts polled by Reuters said they believed that Portugal would not cut its draining or emergency lending rates on Friday at the start of a new commercial bank reserve period, but would wait until after the expected approval of the budget.
